set.body:
DEFECT, independently verified twice (vignette reviewer by rendering, me by reading chunk headers).

vignettes/evidence-pairing.Rmd:36-38 says:

  'The rows below are eight repeated observations and the columns are four native
   neural features. Two sessions remain separate and are combined as declared
   self-products.'

The chunk immediately below, at line 39, is:

  ```{r scalar-data, include=FALSE}

The rows are NOT below. They are suppressed. In the rendered vignette sample_space, native, trend, session1, session2 and signals never appear. The first VISIBLE chunk is at :67 and consumes them:

  :67  ```{r scalar-frame}   ... domain = native ...

A reader copying what the vignette shows them fails on the first visible line with 'object native not found'. The same defect repeats at :321 (cross-domain-setup, include=FALSE) feeding the visible chunk at :349.

This is worse than an ordinary documentation gap because the prose ACTIVELY DIRECTS the reader to content that was deliberately hidden. It is not an omission a reader can route around; it is an instruction to look at something that is not there.

Chunk audit of the file - 8 of 20 chunks are include=FALSE:
  10 setup, 39 scalar-data, 127 scalar-check, 191 multivariate-check,
  219 gaussian-check, 252 rank-one-check, 298 decomposition-check,
  321 cross-domain-setup, 378 cross-domain-check

The *-check chunks are correct usage - they are assertions, and hiding them is right. The two DATA chunks (39, 321) are the defect: they are setup a reader needs, hidden as if they were assertions.

MINIMAL FIX, no restructuring required: change include=FALSE to echo=TRUE on chunks 39 and 321, or move the data construction into a visible chunk and keep only the assertions hidden. This is a two-character-per-chunk edit and it converts the vignette from broken to runnable.

SECOND, SEPARABLE ISSUE in the same file, from the reviewer and worth its own attention: evidence-pairing.Rmd:124 prints edge_000001 / edge_000002 with no indication that edge_000002 is anterior->posterior. The only code mapping edge ids to node names is in the hidden check chunk at :134-138. So the one thing needed to read the output at all is again suppressed. Same class of error: the file consistently hides the interpretive key and shows the opaque result.
set.title: evidence-pairing.Rmd is not copy-pasteable: prose points at rows inside include=FALSE chunks
